title: A human review queue carries no age, no backlog bound, and no default action, so unread items are indistinguishable from approved ones
problem: My agent parks everything it is unsure about in a review queue, and I have no idea whether that queue is being drained, because nothing in the system knows how old the oldest item is.
symptom: The queue directory or table grows without bound while every dashboard stays green. There is no oldest-pending age, no backlog size alarm, and no stated behaviour for an item nobody ever looks at, so a queue that is never read reports exactly the same health as one drained hourly.
why_now: Deferring to a human is the standard 2026 answer to agent uncertainty, and it is treated as the end of the story rather than the start of a queue with a service level. The failure is the documented alert-fatigue outcome arriving through a new door: production is fine, the reviewer is the bottleneck, and no instrument points at the reviewer.
existing: Framework interrupt and resume primitives suspend a run correctly but say nothing about how long a suspended run may wait or what happens if it waits forever.
Generic job-queue metrics measure worker throughput, not the latency of a decision made by a person, so a human queue looks healthy whenever the enqueue side is healthy.
Triage and ranking research reduces the volume of items, which raises the odds any given item is read but still leaves the tail unmeasured.

evidence.title: Towards Better Static Code Analysis Reports: Sentence Transformer-based Filtering of Non-Actionable Alerts
evidence.quote: often contain a large number of non-actionable findings, which can overwhelm developers to the point of ignoring them altogether
evidence.note: arXiv preprint (cs.SE), not stated as peer reviewed. The canonical documented form of this failure: a machine-generated review queue outruns human attention and is then ignored wholesale rather than item by item, which is why per-item quality work does not fix it.

evidence.title: When Errors Become Narratives: A Longitudinal Taxonomy of Silent Failures in a Production LLM Agent Runtime
evidence.quote: we documented 22 incidents with full root-cause postmortems, in which one meta-pattern -- a failure whose error signal never reaches a human in actionable form -- manifested at least 28 times
evidence.note: arXiv preprint reporting 22 root-cause postmortems from a runtime in continuous production. It names the general mechanism this gap is one instance of: the signal is produced and never lands on a human in a form they act on.

build_hypothesis: Give the review queue the same instruments a request queue already has and one a request queue does not: oldest-pending age, backlog size, drain rate, and a declared expiry policy per item so that an unread item resolves to a stated default rather than to silence.

check.manual_question: For the queue this agent parks uncertain items in: what is the age of its oldest unread item right now, what is the alarm threshold on that age, and what happens to an item nobody ever reads?
check.rationale: A codebase that routes work to a human review queue but carries no vocabulary for queue age, backlog size, drain rate or item expiry has no way to observe a queue nobody reads. It can be wrong when the accounting lives outside the repo, in a metrics dashboard or a database view, which is exactly what the manual question exists to settle.
